To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
accounting educators' problem-solving styles were found to be related to their pedagogical preferences.
accounting educators are more adaptive than innovative problem-solvers, and that the problem-solving style is related to pedagogical preferences and perceptions.
accounting faculty are more likely to be adaptive than to be innovative problem solvers.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the problem-solving style that accounting educators use in their professional and academic work, as well as their preferences for certain pedagogy and curricular changes in the education process, which may be affected by their problem-solving style.
the problem-solving style exhibited among accounting educators.
the impact of accounting educators' problem-solving styles on their perceptions of the teaching and learning process.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the accounting educators in this study were adaptive problem solvers who preferred traditional teaching methodologies.

accounting educators who are adaptive problem solvers are more likely to prefer pedagogical methodologies that emphasize the importance of rules, structure and order, and are more likely to perceive that the accounting curriculum should focus on the development of skills and knowledge that are useful in the workplace, and that the accounting profession is a conservative one.
accounting educators' problem-solving styles do not seem to be a significant determinant in their pedagogical preferences and perceptions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
accounting educators' problem-solving styles are associated with pedagogical preferences and may influence their propensity to implement pedagogical and curricular changes.
accounting educators who are adaptive in their problem-solving style are likely to prefer pedagogical approaches that are more structured, traditional, and less student-centered.
accounting educators' problem-solving styles may affect how they perceive and approach the education process.
The main takeaway from our work is that
accounting faculty are not as innovative in problem solving as accounting students and that this may affect the pedagogical approaches used in the accounting classroom.
accounting faculty members' problem-solving styles may affect the way they teach accounting.
educators' problem-solving styles should be considered when designing and implementing innovative pedagogical approaches.
